posts.linkedin:
Freelancers often find a local business on Google Maps but no phone number.

When you search for a cafe, a gym, a clinic or any other small business, the location appears instantly. The website link may open, but the contact page is often hidden or missing, and a working phone number can be hard to locate. You can spend many minutes trying to find a way to reach the business. Often the only way to contact them is to walk to the door.

I create a daily Excel sheet that lists pre‑qualified local businesses. The list is useful for freelancers, agencies and solo service sellers who need local clients. The sheet is compiled from Google Places and includes the business name, address, phone number and a brief note from the website.

The process is simple. First you tell me the type of local businesses you want to target. Then I pull the relevant entries from Google Places, verify the contact details and add a short note from each website. Finally I send you the spreadsheet so you can begin outreach without spending hours on cold searching.

With the sheet you can start sending emails, making calls or sending WhatsApp messages right away. Because the contact information is already gathered, you spend less time hunting for details and more time talking to potential clients. It makes it easier to reach businesses that are visible on Maps but otherwise hard to contact.

The sheet does not guarantee replies or sales, and it does not replace personal follow‑up on complex queries. It is a starting point, not a finished conversation, and you will still need to craft your own messages.

If you think this could fit your outreach workflow, feel free to message me. Payment is required only after you approve the work. DM LEADS and tell me what you sell. 🙂

replies.reply: Hi, good question. Names and contact details come from Google Places plus a note from each website, so it is not random scraping. It still saves hours of manual searching. What do you usually look for first when you find a business?
